headlines.article_text: Stock market today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at the opening bell in New York City on November 10, 2026. Angela Weiss | Afp | Getty Images Stock futures rose slightly on Tuesday night following a losing session in which Nvidia, coupled with hotter-than-expected inflation data, pressured the broader market. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures gained 88 points, or 0.2%. S&P 500 futures climbed 0.2%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.4%. The Dow pulled back more than 150 points in regular trading, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite shed 0.4% and 0.7%, respectively. At the center of the decline was Nvidia . The chipmaker pulled back 5.5%, as CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy weighed on the stock for the second consecutive session. Nvidia's two-day slide pulled the company's market cap down to around $4.07 trillion, its lowest since late March. Equities also fell on Tuesday after the latest U.S. inflation data solidified expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate hike. The consumer price index increased by 0.4% month over month in October , topping expectations. Expectations for a quarter-point rate increase next month rose to about 90% following the release, per the CME Group's FedWatch tool. "Despite some technical uncertainty, higher than desired levels of inflation should keep the Fed in a stance of dissatisfaction with the degree of progress on inflation remaining lackluster, so hiking the Fed Funds policy rate in December is our and the market's base case," wrote Rick Rieder, CIO of global fixed income at BlackRock. "The question now is more of one of the extent of the hike." Comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller also led traders to price in greater chances of a quarter-point move. Traders on Wednesday will keep their eyes on the artificial intelligence trade, after CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue that beat analyst expectations. The report initially sent the neocloud stock slightly higher. 23 Min Ago Here are some key stats from Tuesday's session Stocks fell broadly on Tuesday, with declines in Nvidia and increasing expectations of a Fed rate hike next month dragging investor sentiment. Below are some of the key stats from the session: The Dow fell 0.3% to close at 52,231.89 for its third negative session in four. UnitedHealth had the most positive points impact on the Dow. Caterpillar had the most negative points impact on the Dow. The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to close at 7,520.93 for its first negative session in three. The benchmark closed above its 200-day moving average but below its 50-day average. Despite the decline, the index remains just 4.1% below a record high. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.74% to close at 25,065.87, its first negative session in three. The composite closed below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. CoreWeave beats on revenue and lifts guidance, easing AI slowdown concerns
headlines.summary: CoreWeave's stock has been hammered heading into the neocloud's Q3 earnings report.
headlines.article_text: CoreWeave (CRWV) Q3 earnings report 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points CoreWeave said revenue jumped 168% in the third quarter. Neoclouds like CoreWeave have been under intensifying pressure due to increasing interest rates. The stock has lost about 40% of its value in the past month, alongside a broader slide in the AI infrastructure trade. In this article CRWV Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Michael Intrator, chief executive officer of CoreWeave Inc., during a Bloomberg Television interview during the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos, Switzerland, on Tuesday, Jan. 20, 2026. Chris J. Ratcliffe | Bloomberg | Getty Images CoreWeave reported better-than-expected quarterly revenue and lifted its 2026 guidance on Tuesday, showing that demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure remains strong despite concerns of a market slowdown. The stock advanced in extended trading. The earnings announcement lands at a particularly volatile moment for CoreWeave and its neocloud peers, as the market sours on the AI trade and as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , the central figure in the global buildout, faces a scandal tied to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Here's how the company performed relative to LSEG consensus: Loss per share: 95 cents adjusted vs. $1.16 expected Revenue: $3.66 billion vs. $3.55 billion expected CoreWeave's revenue soared 168% from about $1.36 billion a year earlier, according to a statement. The company recorded a net loss of $709 million, or $1.27 per share, compared to a net loss of $110 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings exclude stock-based compensation. Executives pushed up their forecast for 2026. They now see $1.275 billion to $1.375 billion in adjusted operating income on $13 billion to $13.3 billion in revenue. Analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha were looking for $1.07 billion in adjusted operating income, and analysts polled by LSEG had expected $12.86 billion in 2026 revenue. In August, CoreWeave's 2026 guidance included $960 million to $1.15 billion in adjusted operating income and $12.4 billion to $13.2 billion in revenue. CoreWeave has lost over 40% of its value in the past month, as investors rotate out of companies most closely tied to AI infrastructure. Rising interest rates have pushed lenders out of the market, raising concerns about ongoing access to capital. Some CoreWeave bond yields recently topped 16%. "The business can execute well and still face a tougher financing environment," Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, wrote in an email. "Strong demand is encouraging; the cost and availability of capital remain critical." CoreWeave will get most the capital it needs for 2027 through clients pre-payments and financing from hardware partners, and the company will raise "a limited amount" as well, CEO Mike Intrator told analysts on a conference call. The company plans to raise new debt tied to a set of contracts in the weeks to come, said Nitin Agrawal, its finance chief. "At current yields, we do not intend to issue additional parent-level unsecured debt through 2027," he said. "By contrast, the asset-level secured debt market has remained stable, with our loans continuing to trade around par value." In all, he said he projects under $5 billion in parent-level debt financing through 2027. Fellow neocloud Nebius , whose stock is down by a similar amount, is scheduled to report earnings on Thursday. Nebius shares got a small boost from CoreWeave's results. Both companies and several other providers of cloud-based graphics processing units are particularly reliant on Nvidia, which provides GPUs as well as necessary capital to the whole ecosystem. Nvidia shares have dropped nearly 10% to start the week as the Huang affair raises pressure on the company in Washington, D.C. Nvidia's board said on Tuesday that it hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate Huang and determine whether national security or company secrets were compromised. CoreWeave investors are also looking toward next week, when key customer Anthropic is scheduled to debut on the Nasdaq. In its updated IPO prospectus on Tuesday, Anthropic indicated that it could be valued at around $1.4 trillion after its share sale. Anthropic has signed deals for the construction of entire data centers that will meet its needs. "We see that we're going to have long-term relationships with the AI labs," said Intrator, a CoreWeave co-founder. During the quarter, CoreWeave said it would establish its first data centers in Asia and announced the Forge service for running and evaluating AI models. Management still anticipates 1.85 gigawatts in active power by the end of 2026. CoreWeave is targeting $37 billion to $39 billion in full-year capital expenditures, which would imply 155% growth at the middle of the range. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha were looking for $37.69 billion. CoreWeave owed almost $47 billion in debt at the end of the third quarter, according to the statement. Like its bigger cloud rivals such as Amazon and Oracle , CoreWeave is rushing to bolster computing capacity for clients. But last week, voters in the U.S., where CoreWeave derives most of its revenue, rejected dozens of initiatives on data center development. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated the incumbent, Republican Greg Abbott, after she said Abbott should try to end 20-year tax breaks on large data centers. "So to begin with, we do not anticipate any impact from the seismic regulatory shift that's occurred," Intrator said. Almost all of CoreWeave's power is online or is permitted and under construction, he said. "If data center construction across the sector were to slow, installed compute becomes scarcer, and the knock-on effect is that GPU pricing may stay higher for longer," Intrator said. He said the company does not expect risks to deliveries in 2027 based on construction at permitted locations. "We could sell all of the capacity that we have to current buyers that are in the queue. We are choosing not to," Intrator said. We're choosing to be patient. We're choosing to bring the infrastructure to market when it is further along, because we believe that that will result in better economic output for the outstanding infrastructure that we have." Meanwhile, demand remains robust, with the company now sitting on a $132.5 billion revenue backlog, up from $104 billion as of June . "Should we choose to focus only on our committed backlog, we would expect capex for 2027 to remain in line with our 2026 capex investment, while revenue and EBITDA grow significantly," Agrawal said.
